top3.title: “The Dispossessed” Book Club: Session #8 (Final session)

Le Guin's The Dispossessed — her 1974 anarchist-utopia novel, one of the genre's foundational political texts — closes out with the group landing on the book's ambiguous politics rather than just recapping plot. *(confirm details)*: the listing gives no address beyond "Philadelphia," so confirm the location before heading over.

top3.venue: Iffy Books, 404 S. 20th St., Philadelphia, 19146, United States
top3.why: Iffy Books keeps running some of the city's best hands-on DIY-electronics programming, and this one's a genuine mashup: hand-build a small clay sculpture with an NFC tag embedded inside that can trigger phone shortcuts when tapped. $4.86 covers the clay-and-tag kit; instruction is pay-what-you-can ($5-$15 suggested, notaflof). At the National Constitution Center in Old City, an easy walk from Center City.

top3.title: Justice 101: From Natural Rights to “Slave of the State”- Philadelphia’s Founding Vision and the Making of the “Slave of the Sta
top3.why: Eastern State Penitentiary's lecture series turns its own history inside out this time, tracing a line from Philadelphia's founding "natural rights" rhetoric to the carceral state the city went on to help build — the kind of institution-critiquing public history that's easy to walk past. A one-off talk inside one of the city's most resonant sites for thinking about incarceration and state power. Fairmount — take the 48 bus or walk about 20 minutes from the Broad Street Line's Fairmount Ave stop.

top3.title: Film | Ninotchka

Chestnut Hill — reachable via Regional Rail's Chestnut Hill East Line or the 23 bus up Germantown Ave.

top3.title: Andrzej Żuławski Book Release ft. L’AMOUR BRAQUE (1985)
top3.why: PhilaMOCA screens Andrzej Żuławski's 1985 L'Amour Braque (Mad Love) — one of the wilder entries in the Polish director's hysterical, maximalist filmography — to celebrate critic Samm Deighan's new book on his work, with Deighan herself in the room. Doors/reception at 7, screening introduction at 7:30. Exactly the kind of specialist film-and-literature crossover that justifies PhilaMOCA's whole existence. $12, Callowhill, an easy walk from the Convention Center or Jefferson Station.

Real stakes behind a low-key night of music. Northern Liberties, near the Market-Frankford Line's Girard stop or the 57 bus.
